name: Sheriff's Defense
description: "Why, master," quoth Little John, taking the bags and weighing them in his hand, "here is the chink of gold." The folk hero Robin Hood has been troubling Sheriff of Nottingham greatly. Sheriff knows that Robin Hood is about to attack his camps and he wants to be prepared. Sheriff of Nottingham built the camps with strategy in mind and thus there are exactly $$$n$$$ camps numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ and $$$n-1$$$ trails, each connecting two camps. Any camp can be reached from any other camp. Each camp $$$i$$$ has initially $$$a_i$$$ gold. As it is now, all camps would be destroyed by Robin. Sheriff can strengthen a camp by subtracting exactly $$$c$$$ gold from each of its neighboring camps and use it to build better defenses for that camp. Strengthening a camp doesn't change its gold, only its neighbors' gold. A camp can have negative gold. After Robin Hood's attack, all camps that have been strengthened survive the attack, all others are destroyed. What's the maximum gold Sheriff can keep in his surviving camps after Robin Hood's attack if he strengthens his camps optimally? Camp $$$a$$$ is neighboring camp $$$b$$$ if and only if there exists a trail connecting $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. Only strengthened camps count towards the answer, as others are destroyed.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Each test case begins with two integers $$$n$$$, $$$c$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2\cdot10^5, 1 \le c \le 10^9$$$) — the number of camps and the gold taken from each neighboring camp for strengthening. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$$$ ($$$-10^9 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the initial gold of each camp. Then follow $$$n-1$$$ lines, each with integers $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$, $$$u \ne v$$$) — meaning that there is a trail between $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. The sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$2\cdot10^5$$$. It is guaranteed that any camp is reachable from any other camp.
output_specification: Output a single integer, the maximum gold Sheriff of Nottingham can keep in his surviving camps after Robin Hood's attack.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2014F — Sheriff's Defense [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
